posts.title: Penguin sleep: one block or fragments? Studied nesting chinstrap penguins slept in bouts averaging about four seconds. Libourel et al. · 2023. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Some people punch their partner in their dreams. In REM sleep behaviour disorder the body acts out dreams. In a large study, 73.5% developed Parkinson's or a related disorder within 12 years (Postuma et al., 2019). #remsleep #sleepdisorder #parkinsons #sleepscience

Cavefish versus surface fish: more sleep or less? Three studied cave populations of Mexican tetra slept much less than surface fish of the same species. Duboué et al. · 2011. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Millions have seen him at night. In sleep paralysis you wake up unable to move, and many people see or sense an intruder. About 7.6% of people have had it at least once (Sharpless & Barber, 2011). Have you? #sleepparalysis #shadowman #truestory #sleepscience

Dream about being chased meaning: what science says. In a survey of 1,181 students, being chased was the most common of 55 dream themes (81.5% at least once). One idea is threat rehearsal, still debated. #dreammeaning #beingchased #dreams #nightmares #sleepscience

Teeth falling out dream meaning: what science says. In one study of 210 students, teeth dreams weren't linked to distress or poor sleep, but went with tension in the teeth, gums or jaw on waking. Linked, not proven. #dreammeaning #teethfallingout #dreams #teethdream #sleepscience

People drove cars while fully asleep. In 2019 the FDA added a boxed warning to zolpidem, eszopiclone and zaleplon after 66 serious cases of sleepwalking, sleep driving and other complex sleep behaviours, 20 of them deaths. #truestory #sleepdriving #sleepwalking #sleepscience

Night terrors vs nightmares: what's the difference? Night terrors usually happen early in the night, in deep sleep, and are rarely remembered; nightmares come in dream sleep, later on, and usually are (NHS, AASM). #nightterrors #nightmares #sleep #parenting #sleepscience

There is a disease that ends sleep. Fatal familial insomnia is an inherited prion disease that takes away the ability to sleep. It is extremely rare, and ordinary insomnia does not turn into it. #sleepscience #insomnia #brain #didyouknow

Are you taller in the morning? Yes, by about 2 cm. In a 1984 study, height peaked on waking and was about 1.1% lower by midnight: spine discs lose volume when you are upright and refill when you lie down. It varies by person. #taller #bodyfacts #didyouknow #sleep #spine

She was found asleep on a crane. London, 2005: a sleepwalking 15-year-old climbed a crane and was found asleep about 40 m up. Firefighters brought her down unharmed. #truestory #sleepwalking #london #sleepscience

Does sleep need a central brain? Cassiopea jellyfish showed a sleep-like state without a centralized nervous system. Nath et al. · 2017. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

He killed while asleep. Then he was acquitted. Toronto, 1987: Ken Parks drove to his in-laws' house while sleepwalking. Canada's Supreme Court upheld his acquittal in 1992. Has anyone in your family sleepwalked? #truestory #sleepwalking #truecrime #sleepscience

How long should it take to fall asleep? About 10 to 20 minutes. Dropping off almost instantly, night after night, can be a sign of sleep debt. Fine if you wake refreshed; if you are tired every day, talk to a doctor. #fallasleep #sleeptips #sleepscience #sleep #tired

Why do I wake up at 3am? What sleep science says. Brief wake-ups are normal, 3 to 4 a.m. is a body-clock turning point, and a 2022 hypothesis says night tilts mood negative. If it keeps costing you sleep, talk to a doctor. #3am #cantsleep #insomnia #sleepscience #sleep

Do you swallow spiders in your sleep? Myth check. A spider expert at the Burke Museum (University of Washington) says no case is on formal record, and a sleeper's vibrations tend to warn spiders away. An expert's view, not a study. #spiders #sleepmyths #mythbusting #sleep #didyouknow

Your dreams rarely replay your day. In a 2003 study, 29 people kept a daily log and wrote down dreams for 14 days. About 65% of 299 dream reports were judged to reflect recent life, yet whole-episode replays appeared in no more than 1 to 2%. Pieces, not reruns. #dreams #sleepscience #psychology #brain #didyouknow

Can a brain scan guess what you dream? In a 2013 Science study from Kyoto, a model trained on scans of people looking at pictures picked object categories in sleep-onset imagery from three volunteers, right about 60% of the time on average (chance 50%). Categories, not films. #dreams #sleepscience #neuroscience #brain #didyouknow

You can dream outside REM sleep too. In a 2017 sleep-lab study using high-density EEG, people woken from REM and from non-REM sleep reported dreams, and activity in a back-of-brain hot zone tracked whether they dreamed. One lab, so treat it as a strong clue, not the last word. #dreams #sleepscience #neuroscience #brain #didyouknow

Asleep, your nose is a poor alarm. Your ears aren't. In a small 2004 Brown University lab study (6 young adults), peppermint got no response in deeper sleep and harsh pyridine only some, while a tone got a response on at least 75% of trials. Smoke itself wasn't tested. #sleepscience #sleepfacts #brain #psychology #didyouknow

Falling asleep in under 5 minutes is not a flex. Normal sleep latency is around 10 to 20 minutes. Dropping off almost instantly, night after night, can be a sign of sleep debt rather than great sleep. If it's every night and you're tired by day, talk to a doctor. #sleepscience #fallingasleep #sleepdebt #brain #psychology

Why do your worries feel bigger after midnight? One sleep researcher says 3 to 4 a.m. is a body-clock turning point when we're at our lowest ebb and alone in the dark. A 2022 hypothesis says night tilts mood negative. Brief wake-ups are normal. #3amthoughts #sleepscience #psychology #overthinking #brain

Your brain stays on guard in a new bed. In a 35-person Brown University study, a network in the left half of the brain slept lighter on night one and woke people faster to odd sounds. By night two, the difference was gone. #sleepscience #firstnighteffect #travel #brain #fallingasleep

In mice, sleep widened the gaps between brain cells and waste cleared faster. Sleeping humans show big fluid waves. But a 2024 mouse study found the opposite, so the debate is open. #sleepscience #brain #neuroscience #glymphatic #3amthoughts

It's called exploding head syndrome: a scary name for a painless sleep-onset glitch. In one study, 18% of college students said it had happened to them at least once. #explodingheadsyndrome #sleepscience #fallingasleep #brain #psychology
You dream every REM cycle, but the sleeping brain is bad at saving new memories. People who wake briefly more often tend to remember more. #dreams #dreamscience #sleepscience #remsleep #nightthoughts
It's hypnagogia: the drowsy border where images drift in. Over a third of people report it, and it may even be a creative sweet spot. #hypnagogia #sleepscience #fallingasleep #psychology #dreamy
